The TNT and TNT3c recordings: what is measured

QuestionWhat do the TNT and TNT3c recordings contain, and which numbers are taken from them for the comparison with the model?
Inputs
  • TNT_ovlp16_resp_perfly.pkl and TNT3c_ovlp16_resp_perfly.pkl (Yang, 2026-10-15): per recording, a table of units × 16 odors
  • TNT_ovlp16_cosine_mean_RDM.csv, TNT3c_ovlp16_cosine_mean_RDM.csv: Yang's mean RDMs, used as a check
Outputs
  • odor_weighted/TNT_vs_model_per_odor.csv, TNT_vs_model_odor_pairs.csv (data columns)
  • TNT_data_checks.csv / .json, TNT_rank_order.csv (data rows)
Scripts
  • scripts/tnt_compare.py (section "data" and the helpers)
  • scripts/tnt_data_checks.py
  • scripts/tnt_rank_order.py
  • scripts/reports/r06_tnt_data.py (this report)

Yang recorded KC responses to 16 odors in two genotypes. In TNT, APL's synaptic output is blocked (tetanus toxin light chain expressed in APL). TNT3c is the control, with APL intact (Yang, 2026-10-15). This report describes the files, the quantities taken from them, and how reliable those quantities are. The pickles are read with a restricted loader (scripts/orn_load.py) that only accepts pandas and numpy classes.

1The recordings

There are 8 TNT recordings from 7 flies and 11 TNT3c recordings from 8 flies. A recording name reads date_fly + FL/FR (left or right side) + fun and a number. Where one fly gives two recordings, they are its two hemispheres. The label 20240802_5 appears in both files but names two different flies (Yang). Every recording is a table with one row per unit and one column per odor; the 16 odors are the same, in the same order, as in the ORN table.

2Response values and the "responding" criterion

The file does not state the units of rio(n)r^{(n)}_{io}rio(n)​. The values behave like ΔF/F: most lie near 0, and a minority are large. A unit responds to an odor if its value is above 1. This is the threshold used in all comparisons (0.5 is checked as an alternative):

ϕo(n)=1Nn #{ i:rio(n)>1 },ϕoc=1∣c∣∑n∈cϕo(n)(1)\phi^{(n)}_o = \frac{1}{N_n}\,\#\{\, i : r^{(n)}_{io} > 1 \,\}, \qquad \phi^c_o = \frac{1}{|c|}\sum_{n \in c} \phi^{(n)}_o \tag{1}ϕo(n)​=Nn​1​#{i:rio(n)​>1},ϕoc​=∣c∣1​n∈c∑​ϕo(n)​(1)
NnN_nNn​ = units in recording nnn; ∣c∣|c|∣c∣ = recordings of condition ccc; every recording counts equally
so=ϕoTNTϕoTNT3c(2)s_o = \frac{\phi^{\mathrm{TNT}}_o}{\phi^{\mathrm{TNT3c}}_o} \tag{2}so​=ϕoTNT3c​ϕoTNT​​(2)

On average over odors, 15% of units respond in TNT and 7% in TNT3c. Suppression ranges from ×1.65 (euc) to ×2.90 (eb). Report 07 uses these per-odor fractions to pin the model: with APL blocked, the model responds to each odor in the TNT fraction, and with APL intact its mean equals the TNT3c mean.

3Odor-pair similarity

For each recording, the similarity of two odors is the cosine of their response vectors over all of its units (raw values, not thresholded). The condition's similarity is the mean over its recordings:

Sab(n)=∑iria(n) rib(n)∑i(ria(n))2 ∑i(rib(n))2,Sabc=1∣c∣∑n∈cSab(n)(3)S^{(n)}_{ab} = \frac{\sum_i r^{(n)}_{ia}\, r^{(n)}_{ib}}{\sqrt{\sum_i \big(r^{(n)}_{ia}\big)^2}\,\sqrt{\sum_i \big(r^{(n)}_{ib}\big)^2}}, \qquad S^c_{ab} = \frac{1}{|c|}\sum_{n\in c} S^{(n)}_{ab} \tag{3}Sab(n)​=∑i​(ria(n)​)2​∑i​(rib(n)​)2​∑i​ria(n)​rib(n)​​,Sabc​=∣c∣1​n∈c∑​Sab(n)​(3)

1−Sabc1 - S^c_{ab}1−Sabc​ is exactly Yang's RDM for that condition (checked to 10⁻⁶ for every pair). The effect of blocking APL on a pair is

ΔSab=SabTNT−SabTNT3c(4)\Delta S_{ab} = S^{\mathrm{TNT}}_{ab} - S^{\mathrm{TNT3c}}_{ab} \tag{4}ΔSab​=SabTNT​−SabTNT3c​(4)

All 120 pairs are more similar in TNT. Mean similarity rises from 0.16 to 0.34 (mean ΔS\Delta SΔS = +0.178, range +0.07 to +0.33).

4Splitting the change into per-odor and pair-specific parts

Some odors gain similarity with every partner. To separate that from what is specific to a pair, the change is fitted by least squares as a mean plus one effect per odor:

ΔSab≈μ+ea+eb,∑aea=0(5)\Delta S_{ab} \approx \mu + e_a + e_b, \qquad \sum_a e_a = 0 \tag{5}ΔSab​≈μ+ea​+eb​,a∑​ea​=0(5)
μ\muμ = mean change; eae_aea​ = how much more the pairs of odor aaa change than the average pair

R2R^2R2 of this fit is 0.65: 65% of the variation of ΔS\Delta SΔS across pairs is per odor. The residuals, ΔSab−(μ+ea+eb)\Delta S_{ab} - (\mu + e_a + e_b)ΔSab​−(μ+ea​+eb​), are the pair-specific part.

5How reliable these numbers are

The recordings are the unit of resampling everywhere: bootstrap draws resample recordings with replacement within each condition, and split-half tests divide each condition's recordings into two random halves. A split-half correlation describes half the data. It is turned into an estimate for all the data with the Spearman–Brown formula, rfull=2rhalf/(1+rhalf)r_{\mathrm{full}} = 2r_{\mathrm{half}}/(1 + r_{\mathrm{half}})rfull​=2rhalf​/(1+rhalf​).

  • Rank order of similarity. Over the 120 pairs, STNTS^{\mathrm{TNT}}STNT and STNT3cS^{\mathrm{TNT3c}}STNT3c have ρs\rho_sρs​ = 0.87. With half the recordings, two halves of the same condition give 0.90 (TNT3c) and 0.91 (TNT), while TNT vs TNT3c gives 0.83. The between-condition value is lower in 97.5% of splits. Dividing the between-condition value by the within-condition one gives about 0.92: the rank correlation expected without measurement noise. Report 09 and the local model use this as the data's value.
  • Change per pair. The split-half reliability of ΔS\Delta SΔS caps any model's correlation with it near r = 0.84 (Report 07).
  • Duplicates. No unit is repeated within or across recordings. Units whose nearest neighbour in their own recording is closer than expected are rare (0.5% of responsive TNT units, 1.6% TNT3c).
  • Two hemispheres of one fly. Weighting each fly once instead of each recording changes the mean ΔS\Delta SΔS from 0.178 to 0.182, and the pattern over pairs correlates 0.99.
Caveats

The units are not matched across recordings or conditions, so every comparison is between condition means.

Response units are not stated. Thresholding at 1 assumes the values are on a comparable scale in both genotypes.

Noise lowers cosine similarity more when responses are small. TNT3c has smaller responses, so part of the rise in TNT may be noise. Thresholding at 1 before the cosine gives the same picture (every pair still rises; pattern r 0.94 with the raw change).
